title: NOT VIETNAMESE
sub: For more than a thousand years, a kingdom on Vietnam's coast spoke a language from a different family than Vietnamese.
say: For more than a thousand years, a kingdom on Vietnam's coast spoke a language from a different family than Vietnamese.

title: AUSTRONESIAN
sub: The Cham spoke an Austronesian language. Its closest relatives are not Vietnamese or Khmer, but languages like Acehnese and Malay, spoken across the sea.
say: The Chahm spoke an Austronesian language. Its closest relatives are not Vietnamese or Khmer, but languages like Ah-chay-neez and Malay, spoken across the sea.

title: SANSKRIT + CHAM
sub: Their inscriptions were written in Sanskrit, the classical language of India, and in Old Cham.
say: Their inscriptions were written in Sanskrit, the classical language of India, and in Old Chahm.

title: ĐÔNG YÊN CHÂU
sub: One Old Cham stone, from Đông Yên Châu, is often described as one of the oldest known texts in any Austronesian language. Its exact date is still studied.
say: One Old Chahm stone, from Dong Yen Chow, is often described as one of the oldest known texts in any Austronesian language. Its exact date is still studied.

title: AKHAR THRAH
sub: And the Cham script, Akhar Thrah, is still taught in some village schools.
say: And the Chahm script, Ah-kar Trah, is still taught in some village schools.

title: HOW?
sub: So how did a kingdom like this become part of Vietnam?
say: So how did a kingdom like this become part of Vietnam?
